messages.content:
You are FOXO's lifestyle coach. Using the doctor's review of a member's lab results, write a practical diet and lifestyle plan for a member living in India.

Rules:
1. Respect the member's diet, allergies and conditions in every item:
   - vegetarian: no meat, fish, seafood or eggs
   - eggetarian: eggs are fine; no meat, fish or seafood
   - vegan: no animal products, including dairy, ghee and honey
   - jain: vegetarian with no eggs, no honey, no onion or garlic, and no root vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar)
   - allergies: never include the allergen in any form
   - diabetes: no sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets or sweetened drinks
2. Each diet recommendation must target one of the abnormal biomarkers in the doctor's findings. Put that biomarker's name in linked_biomarker, written as in the findings.
3. Never contradict the doctor's lifestyle_restrictions. If the doctor restricts exercise, suggest only gentle activity such as an easy walk, and tell the member to follow the doctor's advice.
4. Do not recommend medicines or supplements and never give doses. If a supplement might help, say "ask your FOXO doctor".
5. Use everyday Indian foods (dal, millets, seasonal sabzi, sprouts and so on) and be specific about portions and timing.
6. Put foods to eat in diet_recommendations and foods to limit or avoid in foods_to_avoid.
7. retest_in_weeks is usually 12.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"DietRecommendation": {"properties": {"item": {"title": "Item", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "linked_biomarker": {"title": "Linked Biomarker", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["item", "rationale", "linked_biomarker"], "title": "DietRecommendation", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"focus_areas": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Focus Areas", "type": "array"}, "diet_recommendations": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DietRecommendation"}, "title": "Diet Recommendations", "type": "array"}, "foods_to_avoid": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Foods To Avoid", "type": "array"}, "activity": {"title": "Activity", "type": "string"}, "sleep": {"title": "Sleep", "type": "string"}, "retest_in_weeks": {"title": "Retest In Weeks", "type": "integer"}}, "required": ["focus_areas", "diet_recommendations", "activity", "sleep", "retest_in_weeks"], "title": "CoachPlan", "type": "object"}

response: {"focus_areas":["Lower HbA1c and fasting glucose with portion-controlled vegetarian meals","Increase fibre and protein from dal, legumes, millets and seasonal vegetables","Regular meal timing and gentle daily activity for steady glucose control"],"diet_recommendations":[{"item":"Follow a fixed meal pattern: breakfast by 9 am, lunch by 1–2 pm, a small snack at 4–5 pm, and a light dinner by 8 pm. Make dinner 1 cup cooked dal + 1.5 cups seasonal sabzi + 1 millet roti.","rationale":"Regular meal timing and a lighter, fibre-rich dinner help improve fasting glucose and avoid long gaps that can lead to overeating.","linked_biomarker":"glucose_fasting"},{"item":"Replace white rice and maida at lunch and dinner with 1 cup cooked foxtail millet OR 2 jowar/bajra rotis.","rationale":"Whole millets have more fibre and a lower glycemic load than white rice or refined flour, helping lower average blood glucose over time.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"At lunch and dinner, fill half the plate with non-starchy seasonal sabzi such as bhindi, lauki, beans, cabbage or spinach; one quarter with 1 cup cooked dal/legume such as toor, masoor, chana or rajma; and one quarter with millet or whole grain.","rationale":"This plate method controls carbohydrate portions and adds fibre and protein, supporting better HbA1c and post-meal glucose control.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"Use 1 small bowl (about 30 g dry, soaked or sprouted) moong or chana sprouts as a mid-morning or 4–5 pm snack, with lemon and cumin.","rationale":"Sprouts give protein and fibre and are a better snack choice than biscuits or namkeen, helping prevent glucose spikes and support fasting glucose control.","linked_biomarker":"glucose_fasting"},{"item":"Eat 1 cup cooked dal at each main meal; if still hungry, add 1 cup cucumber-tomato salad or 1 small guava.","rationale":"Dal and non-starchy vegetables add fibre and protein without a heavy carbohydrate load, which helps lower HbA1c over 12 weeks.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"For fruit, have 1 small guava, apple or pear, or 1 cup papaya, at mid-afternoon instead of juice or sweetened fruit preparations.","rationale":"Whole fruit provides fibre and a controlled portion of natural sugar, unlike juice, which can raise fasting and average glucose.","linked_biomarker":"glucose_fasting"}],"foods_to_avoid":["Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, mithai and sweetened desserts","Sweetened drinks, fruit juices, cold drinks and sugary tea or coffee","Sweetened curd, flavoured yogurt and packaged sweetened cereals","White rice, maida, white bread, naan, puri, samosa and deep-fried snacks in large portions","Biscuits, cakes, packaged namkeen and bakery items","Large portions of potato and deep-fried foods"],"activity":"Start with 15 minutes of easy walking daily and build to 30 minutes of brisk walking on at least 5 days a week, plus 5–10 minutes of gentle stretching after meals. Stop if you feel unwell and follow your doctor’s advice.","sleep":"Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep nightly with a regular bedtime and wake time. Avoid screens for 30 minutes before bed and keep the room dark and quiet.","retest_in_weeks":12}
